analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and metadata against the canonical definition index and selected detailed evidence. CoordinatorClient.swift:120–141 adds an injectable reconnect policy; CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift:12–43 replaces exponential backoff with randomized policy-selected delays. Connection.swift:164–165 starts duration measurement after registration is sent, not after serving authorization. The new lock-protected CoordinatorSessionRecorder in CoordinatorClientState.swift:514–536 transfers duration and close-code observations from transport callbacks to the actor. Connection.swift:397–400 records close codes even on receive errors; :492–500 safely reads a two-byte fallback code only when sufficient payload exists.
No supported security regression was identified in this scope. Close-code observations affect reconnect timing, not trust or permission. Existing TLS selection, inbound size cap, fresh socket nonce, connection-identity checks, teardown and drain failure handling remain intact in the supplied surrounding source. No changed prompt encryption, cache storage/scoping (T-041), model integrity, billing, credential custody or privileged-helper behavior was observed. Relevant interactions are availability at TB-002/A-018 and connection-bound authorization at TB-011/T-053/T-057.
Integration must examine the omitted CoordinatorReconnectPolicy/CoordinatorSessionEnd implementation: verify finite valid delay ranges, bounded retries under repeated short sessions and close codes, and whether treating registration-send duration as session health permits retry amplification. Also reconcile close-code availability when the terminal-state monitor races the receive callback (Connection.swift:148–150, 214–229, 397–405). These are unverified contracts, not established vulnerabilities. Unchanged authorization/admission callers were not reviewed; no full audit or deployment conclusion is implied.
